title: Zumbi dos Palmares
summary: Born in 1655 in the Palmares quilombo, Zumbi was captured as a child and sold, then escaped at fifteen and returned to Palmares, a large community of fugitive Africans and their descendants in Alagoas, in colonial Pernambuco. He became a military leader and its last king. Colonial forces destroyed Palmares in 1695; he was found and killed on 20 November 1695, a date now marked in Brazil.

uncertainty.note: The Encyclopedia of Invisibility gives his birth as 1655 and his death as 20 November 1695; Encyclopedia.com gives 20 November 1695 and does not state a birth date. The Encyclopedia of Invisibility also says Palmares fell in 1694 while giving 1695 for his death.

where.modern_name: Serra da Barriga, União dos Palmares, Alagoas, Brazil (pinned to the ridge where the main Palmares quilombos stood and where a monument to him stands; the sources do not name the place of his death)
where.historical_name: Serra da Barriga in the captaincy of Pernambuco, colonial Brazil, site of the quilombo of Palmares

importance.justification: Both sources present him as the leader of Palmares at its end and as a symbol of resistance whose death date is now a Brazilian day of commemoration.

audience_note: This record covers enslavement, the capture and sale of a child, a military campaign and a killing; the sources note that his body was decapitated.

reviewer_note: Birth year (1655) rests on a single source of class other. The sources disagree on when Palmares fell (1694 vs 1695). No standalone Palmares record exists in the atlas yet, so it is not linked. The pin is a ridge, not a death site.
